say.en: Need 6 microfarads but only have 2 microfarads capacitors? Join them. But be careful: capacitors combine the opposite way to resistors. In this lesson: Find the equivalent capacitance of series and parallel combinations.
Find the energy stored in a capacitor and the energy density of the field.

body.en: *Series*: the same charge Q sits on every capacitor and the voltages add, so $1/C_s = 1/C_1 + 1/C_2 + \dots$; the result is smaller than the smallest capacitor. Parallel: the same V is across each and the charges add, so $C_p = C_1 + C_2 + \dots$.
body.kn: ಶ್ರೇಣಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಎಲ್ಲಾ ಧಾರಕಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಒಂದೇ ಆವೇಶ; 1/C ಕೂಡುತ್ತದೆ. ಸಮಾಂತರದಲ್ಲಿ ಎಲ್ಲದರ ಮೇಲೆ ಒಂದೇ V; C ನೇರವಾಗಿ ಕೂಡುತ್ತದೆ.

narration.en: In series every capacitor has the same charge and one over C adds. In parallel every capacitor has the same voltage and C simply adds.

title.en: On the board: combining capacitors and stored energy

narration.en: In series the same charge Q sits on every capacitor, and the voltages add. In parallel every capacitor has the same voltage V, and the charges add. Example: 2 μF and 3 μF give 1.2 μF in series and 5 μF in parallel. Charging a capacitor: V rises in step with Q, and the area under the V–Q line is the stored energy. So U = ½QV = ½CV² = Q²/2C, and the energy per unit volume of the field is ½ε₀E². Example: 1.2 μF charged to 10 V stores one half times 1.2 times 100, that is 60 microjoule.

say.en: In series the same charge Q sits on every capacitor, and the voltages add.
In parallel every capacitor has the same voltage V, and the charges add.
Example: 2 μF and 3 μF give 1.2 μF in series and 5 μF in parallel.
Charging a capacitor: V rises in step with Q, and the area under the V–Q line is the stored energy.
So U = ½QV = ½CV² = Q²/2C, and the energy per unit volume of the field is ½ε₀E².
Example: 1.2 μF charged to 10 V stores one half times 1.2 times 100, that is 60 microjoule.

In series the same charge Q sits on every capacitor, and the voltages add. In parallel every capacitor has the same voltage V, and the charges add. Example: 2 microfarads and 3 microfarads give 1.2 microfarads in series and 5 microfarads in parallel. Charging a capacitor: V rises in step with Q, and the area under the V-Q line is the stored energy. So U equals one half QV equals one half CV squared equals Q squared/2C, and the energy per unit volume of the field is one half epsilon 0E squared. Example: 1.2 microfarads charged to 10 volts stores one half times 1.2 times 100, that is 60 microjoule.

narration.en: In series every capacitor carries the same charge and the voltages add: 1/C = 1/C1 + 1/C2. In parallel every capacitor has the same voltage and the charges add: C = C1 + C2. The bars show the charge on each. Stored energy U = ½CV².
narration.kn: ಶ್ರೇಣಿ ಮತ್ತು ಸಮಾಂತರದಲ್ಲಿ ಧಾರಕಗಳು. ಸ್ಲೈಡರ್‌ಗಳನ್ನು ಸರಿಸಿ, ಓದುಗಳು ಹೇಗೆ ಬದಲಾಗುತ್ತವೆ ಎಂದು ಗಮನಿಸಿ.

say.en: In series every capacitor carries the same charge and the voltages add: 1 over C equals 1 over C1 plus 1 over C2. In parallel every capacitor has the same voltage and the charges add: C equals C1 plus C2. The bars show the charge on each. Stored energy U equals one half CV squared.

body.en: Charging a capacitor takes work, which is stored as *energy* in the electric field between the plates: $U = \frac12CV^2 = \frac{Q^2}{2C} = \frac12QV$. The energy per unit volume of the field is $u = \frac12\varepsilon_0E^2$.
body.kn: ಧಾರಕವನ್ನು ಆವೇಶಗೊಳಿಸಲು ಮಾಡಿದ ಕೆಲಸ ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರದಲ್ಲಿ ಶಕ್ತಿಯಾಗಿ ಸಂಗ್ರಹವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ: U = ½CV² = Q²/2C. ಶಕ್ತಿ ಸಾಂದ್ರತೆ u = ½ε₀E².

narration.en: The work done in charging a capacitor is stored in its field: half C V squared, or Q squared by 2C. The energy density of the field is half epsilon nought E squared.

problem.en: Capacitors of 2 μF, 3 μF and 6 μF are joined (a) in series and (b) in parallel. Find the equivalent capacitance, and the charge on each in series across 12 V.

steps.en: In series across 12 V: Q = 1 μF × 12 V = 12 μC on each capacitor.

answer.en: 1 μF (series), 11 μF (parallel); 12 μC on each in series

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Capacitors of 2 μF, 3 μF and 6 μF are joined (a) in series and (b) in parallel. Find the equivalent capacitance, and the charge on each in series across 12 V.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Capacitors of 2 microfarads, 3 microfarads and 6 microfarads are joined a in series and b in parallel. Find the equivalent capacitance, and the charge on each in series across 12 volts.
Series: 1 over C equals 1 over 2 plus 1 over 3 plus 1 over 6 equals 1, so C equals 1 microfarad.
Parallel: C equals 2 plus 3 plus 6 equals 11 microfarads.
In series across 12 volts: Q equals 1 microfarad times 12 volts equals 12 micro C on each capacitor.
So the answer is 1 microfarad series, 11 microfarads parallel; 12 micro C on each in series.

problem.en: A 12 pF capacitor is connected to a 50 V battery. How much energy is stored?

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A 12 pF capacitor is connected to a 50 V battery. How much energy is stored?

say.en: Let us solve this together. A 12 picofarads capacitor is connected to a 50 volts battery. How much energy is stored?
U equals one half CV squared.
U equals one half times 12 times 10 to the power minus 12 times 50 squared.
U equals 6 times 10 to the power minus 12 times 2500 equals 1.5 times 10 to the power minus 8 joules.
So the answer is 1.5 times 10 to the power minus 8 joules.

heading.en: Product over sum, and n equal capacitors

body.en: Two capacitors in series: C = C₁C₂/(C₁ + C₂). n equal capacitors C: series gives C/n, parallel gives nC. Capacitors in series follow the resistor-in-parallel rule, and vice versa.
